## Scientific question

This preregistered first aspect asks whether SBayesR-LV uses the same frozen
annotation information productively relative to ordinary SBayesR, and whether
its downstream inference resembles SBayesRC while its simpler annotation
posterior is better behaved. It is one simulation, not a general model ranking.

## Frozen design and provenance

All three arms use the exact immutable Study 10 simulation: 4,500 training
people, 500 validation people, 35,000 markers in 35 blocks, target h2 0.5,
and realized component counts 33,989/502/305/204. Every arm uses the same
summary statistics, marker order, validation set, LD reference, and retained
block-eigen contract. The implementation is `sblr` 0.2.0 at qualified SHA
`2123699a9cc2e91059e7d81a745420b14eca7f6e` loaded from an isolated library.

The common schedule is four independent chains, 9,000 total iterations,
3,000 burn-in, 6,000 retained draws, and thinning one. LV fixes
`theta_prior_sd=0.7`; RC uses the preregistered Study 10 proper-intercept,
`a=2,b=2` hierarchy.

## Annotation architecture and convergence

```{r}
knitr::kable(theta, digits = 4)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "theta_forest.png"),
  rel_path = FALSE)
```

The LV binary coefficient is an annotated-versus-unannotated conditional
prior-variance ratio after exponentiation. Continuous coefficients are +1 SD
ratios. Theta stability is interpreted jointly with the marker-scale q
chain-stability evidence, not from R-hat alone.

```{r}
knitr::kable(q_stability, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(q_scalar, digits = 4)
```

LV recovers both informative directions and leaves the null coefficient near
zero. All theta R-hats are below 1.05, but the two informative coefficients
have only about 92--110 bulk effective draws. Marker-q rankings are extremely
stable across chains, whereas their absolute scale remains chain-sensitive.
Accordingly this is useful but not fully settled annotation inference.

SBayesRC alpha is a different estimand. Its raw coefficients and its induced
marker/component prior stability are therefore reported separately.

```{r}
knitr::kable(alpha, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(rc_stability, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(rc_scalar, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "rc_alpha_forest.png"),
  rel_path = FALSE)
```

RC raw alpha is not converged (R-hats up to 1.79; minimum bulk ESS about 5.9).
The instability materially reaches the expected-active architecture
(R-hat 1.57), although component-prior chain means remain highly correlated
and downstream effects are more stable than alpha.

## Variance components, prediction, and runtime

```{r}
knitr::kable(genomic, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(variance, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(runtime_efficiency, digits = 3)
```

The completed R/LV/RC wall times were 5,318.58, 2,555.93, and 3,254.69
seconds. The compact diagnostic probe is kept separate from the scientific
comparison:

```{r}
knitr::kable(runtime_audit, digits = 3)
```

Its 1- and 200-iteration rows are nonmonotone because repeated low-rank
construction and machine cache state dominate such short probes; they are not
used as subtractive per-iteration estimates and did not change the design.

## Interpretation and limitations

The evidence supports preregistered Outcome 3. RC has the best beta truth
correlation (0.812), lowest beta RMSE, and best validation genetic-value
correlation (0.810), so annotation-dependent component membership extracts
information that simple variance modulation does not fully capture here. LV
nevertheless improves over R in beta recovery and validation prediction while
showing much better low-dimensional annotation behavior than RC.

The latent architectures are not interchangeable: R--LV PIPs remain close,
whereas RC PIPs differ substantially from both, even though beta estimates are
more concordant. RC's raw-alpha and expected-active instability therefore
cannot be hidden, but it is progressively attenuated in beta and prediction.
LV theta is much better behaved, yet its low ESS and chain-dependent q
amplitude prevent a claim of fully stable annotation inference.

This is one SBayesRC-generated canonical simulation and does not establish
universal superiority or calibration. No Aspect 2 work was launched.
